title: Topotecan capsules · small-cell lung cancer
purpose: This treatment aims to slow or shrink small-cell lung cancer that has returned after treatment, when repeating the first treatment is not appropriate. Benefit varies; your team explains the aim for you.

agents.name: Topotecan capsules
agents.explanation: Topotecan blocks topoisomerase I, an enzyme that relieves strain while DNA is copied. Unrepaired DNA breaks can stop dividing cancer cells; healthy blood-forming and gut cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Call oncology immediately for fever or suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, severe tummy pain, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or new cough or breathlessness. Do not wait for the next cycle. Contact the team immediately for more than 3 episodes of diarrhoea in a day, or sooner if you feel unwell.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and mouth soreness
Rare severe bowel inflammation or perforation

schedule_summary: Take the prescribed topotecan capsules once daily on Days 1–5 of a 21-day cycle. Days 6–21 have no planned topotecan. Up to 6 cycles are planned, with earlier changes if needed.
administration_text: Swallow capsules whole with water; do not open, chew or crush them. Topotecan can be taken with or without food. Keep it refrigerated at 2–8°C; do not freeze. The pharmacy label gives the exact strengths and number of capsules.

support.title: Sickness and bowel symptoms
support.text: Use your prescribed prevention or rescue medicine. Report persistent vomiting, diarrhoea or inability to drink; fever with severe tummy pain needs urgent assessment.

support.title: Blood tests and review
support.text: Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before treatment and before each cycle. Extra tests depend on symptoms and results.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and medicines
support.text: Discuss fertility and contraception before treatment. Tell the team about pregnancy, breastfeeding, all medicines, supplements and vaccines. Check before changing any medicine.

support.title: Missed or vomited capsules
support.text: Do not double a missed dose or take replacement capsules after vomiting without team advice. Record what happened, contact the oncology pharmacist/team, and follow the next scheduled dose in the agreed plan.

support.title: Safe handling
support.text: Swallow capsules whole with water; do not open, chew or crush them. Topotecan can be taken with or without food. Keep it refrigerated at 2–8°C; do not freeze. The pharmacy label gives the exact strengths and number of capsules. Keep away from children; ask the pharmacy how to return unused or damaged capsules.

questions.a: Blood results or symptoms may make a delay or dose change safer. Your team confirms when to restart.

questions.q: Are capsules gentler than an infusion?
questions.a: No. Oral chemotherapy can cause serious toxicity and needs blood tests and review. Oral and intravenous doses cannot be exchanged.
Your consultant sets the timing for your disease and treatment plan. No universal scan or tumour-marker interval is specified here.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be offered
evidence.summary: An older randomized trial found longer survival and slower loss of quality of life when oral topotecan was added to supportive care in patients unsuitable for standard intravenous treatment.
evidence.intro: An older randomized trial found longer survival and slower loss of quality of life when oral topotecan was added to supportive care in patients unsuitable for standard intravenous treatment.
evidence.caveat: These historical groups do not predict an individual outcome or compare every treatment available today. Treatment choice also depends on previous response, time since treatment, fitness and preferences.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment days
chronology_notes.text: Take the prescribed topotecan capsules once daily on Days 1–5 of a 21-day cycle. Days 6–21 have no planned topotecan. Up to 6 cycles are planned, with earlier changes if needed.

chronology_notes.title: Between cycles
chronology_notes.text: Tiredness, sickness, mouth or bowel symptoms may occur during treatment and afterwards. Timing varies. Blood counts can fall after dosing ends; fever, bleeding or feeling suddenly unwell needs an immediate call. Recovery is checked before another cycle; no calendar day guarantees that your counts or symptoms have recovered.

chronology_notes.title: Checks and next steps
chronology_notes.text: Keep planned tests and appointments. Scans and follow-up are individually arranged.

monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney and liver tests before treatment and before each cycle. Scans and follow-up follow the consultant plan.
